title: TAG: Tangential Amplifying Guidance for Hallucination-Resistant Sampling
claim: Amplifying the tangential component of the update keeps trajectories on the data manifold and recovers the true structure better than other guidance.
layout: Top row of five toy-sample panels with zoom insets; bottom manifold diagram with legend
description: The figure has two parts. The top row shows 2-D toy tree-shaped data in five panels: no guidance, naive truncation, CFG, TAG (Ours) and Ground Truth. The grey tree is the full data manifold, and black dots are generated samples. Each panel has a navy zoom inset on one branch region. The no-guidance and CFG panels show stray outlier points and missing or distorted branches. The TAG panel closely matches the ground truth, with few outliers. Below is a geometric sketch of curved manifolds M_{k+1}, M_k and M_0 with red tangent lines. A blue DDIM arrow and an orange TAG arrow start from the same point, and a purple guidance arrow η points along the tangent. Dotted lines lead toward M_0. A boxed legend explains the colors. The eye goes first to the zoom insets.
caption: Conceptual visualization of Tangential Amplifying Guidance (TAG) from a mode-interpolation perspective [ref]. Unlike (a) no guidance case, (b) TAG decomposes the base increment $\Delta_{k+1}$ on the latent sphere into parallel $\mP_{\mathcal{M}_{k+1}}\Delta_{k+1}$ and orthogonal (i.e., tangential) $\mP_{\mathcal{M}_{k+1}}^\perp\Delta_{k+1}$ components ([ref]). By preserving the parallel component while adding a scaled tangential component, TAG isolates the data-relevant part of the update ([ref]) and can more effectively navigate the data manifold, leading to samples that contain more semantic structure. We make this precise by proving that amplifying the tangential component has the effect of guiding the trajectories toward regions of higher model density while mitigating off-manifold drift ([ref]).
abstract: Diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art image generation but often produce semantic inconsistencies, or hallucinations. Existing inference-time guidance methods rely on external signals or architectural modifications, adding computational overhead. We propose $\mathbf{T}$angential $\mathbf{A}$mplifying $\mathbf{G}$uidance $\mathbf{(TAG)}$, a training-free, architecture-agnostic, plug-and-play guidance method that operates purely on trajectory signals. TAG uses an intermediate sample as a projection basis and amplifies the tangential components of the estimated score to correct the sampling trajectory. A first-order Taylor analysis shows that this steers the state toward higher-probability regions of the data manifold, reducing inconsistencies and improving fidelity while adding negligible overhead to existing samplers. Code is available at our Project Page (https://hyeon-cho.github.io/TAG/).
